title: Asking If It Was Okay with Nothing to Offer
description:
The day they decided to be together, {name} asked Dae-un honestly, 'I have nothing to offer yet — is that okay?'

That honest confession comes back sometimes.

Today Dae-un brought up that day.

choices.text: "Glad I was honest back then."
choices.result_text:
'You said you had nothing to offer — but the honesty was the biggest thing.'

A relationship begun without pretense stayed sturdy even when shaken.
{name} knows the honesty of that starting point protected them both.

choices.text: "Now — I've become someone who can offer a little."
choices.result_text:
'I had enough back then too.'

They were empty-handed then, but the heart was real.
{name} can now add a little means to that heart, bit by bit.

title: Asking Where We're Going
description:
When things were uncertain, {name} asked Dae-un first, 'Where are we going with this?'

That courageous question comes back sometimes.

Today they think about the two of them's future again.

choices.text: Asking then — set our direction
choices.result_text:
Asking directly rather than enduring the ambiguity.

That question pulled the relationship out of vagueness.
{name} felt that moment of facing it instead of avoiding was right.

choices.text: Even now — I don't put off saying what matters
choices.result_text:
Don't ask and there's no answer.

{name} decided, as learned then, not to put off what matters.
That question taught that relationships grow on clarity.

title: We're Going Together, We Said
description:
A few years in, {name} and Dae-un steadied each other — 'we're going together.'

That promise of companionship comes back sometimes.

Today is the end of another day endured together.

choices.text: Because we're together — I could come this far
choices.result_text:
Alone, it was a road that would have broken them several times.

With someone walking beside, {name} found the strength to go all the way.
Love wasn't a burden, but sharing the same weight.

choices.text: I want to see the end of this road — together
choices.result_text:
The closer the arrival, the clearer the scenery seen together.

{name} went further wanting to see that end with Dae-un.
Arriving alone and arriving together — the same place, yet different.

title: Saying Four Years Is a Long Time
description:
While studying together, {name} shared candid feelings with Hyun-su — 'four years is a long time.'

That sincere talk comes back sometimes.

Thoughts of Hyun-su came today.

choices.text: That candid talk — brought us close
choices.result_text:
A conversation showing your insides without pretense deepens a relationship.

{name} and Hyun-su became real friends that way.
Even in a tiny goshiwon, honesty was a bridge between people.

choices.text: Grateful — to who we were back then
choices.result_text:
In a bleak time, listening to each other's hearts was great comfort.

{name} felt grateful to those two.
Memories of enduring together in the same place were a lasting asset.

title: Celebrating Hyun-su's Pass
description:
When Hyun-su passed, {name} celebrated genuinely.

That moment of joy comes back sometimes.

Today Hyun-su checked in.

choices.text: "Your passing — felt like my own."
choices.result_text:
'You congratulated me first, hyung. I won't forget that.'

Being able to rejoice at another's success without envy.
{name} knows that's proof of a truly close bond.

choices.text: "We're both — doing well our own ways."
choices.result_text:
'Right, hyung. Us in our own ways.'

A bond that roots for each other even on different paths.
Starting in the same goshiwon, each going well in their own way.

title: My Past Self Wasn't Wrong, I Said
description:
Looking at an old notebook, {name} accepted, 'my past self wasn't wrong — only the direction changed.'

That reconciliation comes back sometimes.

Today they look back on past choices again.

choices.text: Every choice I made — built the present me
choices.result_text:
Regretted choices and proud ones are all part of me.

{name} accepted their past self instead of condemning it.
Only one reconciled with themselves could walk forward lightly.

choices.text: Only the direction changed — same now
choices.result_text:
Not wrong, just different.

{name} sees the present change the same way.
Constantly adjusting direction wasn't error, but proof of being alive.

title: Saying I Don't Know What Success Is
description:
Asked what success is, {name} answered, 'honestly I don't know yet.'

That honest not-knowing comes back sometimes.

Today they think again about 'what am I heading toward.'

choices.text: Now I know a little — success isn't just a number
choices.result_text:
₩3 billion is a goal, but it wasn't the whole of success.

{name} knows a life unchased, a life with people beside you, is part of success too.
Time spent carrying the question slowly built an answer.

choices.text: Still haven't defined it — and that's okay
choices.result_text:
Not having defined success doesn't mean being lost.

{name} walked well even without a fixed answer.
Some questions you carry for life, and that was okay too.

title: Starting the Job Search
description:
Shocked by the salary gap, {name} started preparing to switch jobs.

That resolve comes back sometimes.

Today they review the direction of their career again.

choices.text: Moving then — prevented stagnation
choices.result_text:
Shocked by reality and sitting still, they'd have stayed there.

{name} turned that shock into action.
Not stopping at admitting the gap, they moved to close it.

choices.text: Prepare steadily — without rushing
choices.result_text:
A job switch should be the result of preparation, not impulse.

{name} chose steady preparation over haste.
Move but not recklessly — that balance led to a better place.

title: Deciding to Be Honest
description:
When {name} learned the secret of the parents' bankbook, they decided 'to be honest when Dad comes back.'

That resolve comes back sometimes.

Today they sit across from Dad again.

choices.text: Choosing honesty then — protected the relationship
choices.result_text:
Hiding it might have been easier. But honesty kept the trust.

{name} knows honesty is needed most among family.
A buried secret would have ultimately made a greater distance.

choices.text: Decide to carry the family's burden — together
choices.result_text:
Knowing the parents' situation, they couldn't pretend not to.

{name} decided not to let them carry that burden alone.
One reason for heading to Gangnam was, in the end, those people.

title: The Vow Never to Return
description:
After a big loss in Jeongseon, boarding the bus, {name} vowed, 'never again, for real.'

Was that vow kept?

Today gambling's temptation beckons from afar.

choices.text: I kept — that vow
choices.result_text:
The vow made on the bus, {name} kept.

A vow isn't spoken but kept daily.
That last bus from Jeongseon was the starting line of a different life.

choices.text: When shaken — I recall that bus
choices.result_text:
Temptation never fully vanishes. But it became manageable.

Whenever shaken, {name} recalls the self on that bus.
The memory of seeing the bottom held them back from that road again.

title: Deciding to Keep Distance
description:
Feeling the warning of addiction, {name} decided 'to keep some distance, not to go for a month.'

That self-awareness comes back sometimes.

Today they sense that temptation's signal again.

choices.text: Keeping distance myself — protected me
choices.result_text:
Addiction wasn't an inability to quit, but an inability to keep distance.

{name} sensed the danger early and stopped themselves.
The ability to see one's state objectively was the most powerful brake.

choices.text: That sense of awareness — I still use
choices.result_text:
The antenna that catches danger signals saved {name} several times.

Not just gambling — the same sense worked before reckless investing or overwork.
The power to monitor oneself was a survival skill that worked anywhere.

title: Enrolling in the English Class
description:
{name} once enrolled in an English class, calling it 'an investment.'

That resolve to learn comes back sometimes.

Today they stand at a self-development fork.

choices.text: Investing in myself — was the surest investment
choices.result_text:
Stocks rise and fall, but what's learned doesn't vanish.

{name} knows investing in their own capacity was the safest asset.
The market may betray you, but skill doesn't.

choices.text: Check if I enrolled and never did it
choices.result_text:
Enrolling is payment, not willpower.

{name} honestly reviewed whether they'd finished what they started.
Real investment wasn't the enrollment fee, but the time steadily put in.

title: Buying the Coding Course
description:
{name} once bought a coding course, calling it 'a ₩1,900 investment.'

That small start comes back sometimes.

Today they consider learning a new skill.

choices.text: Starting even small — opened possibilities
choices.result_text:
Where a ₩1,900 start would lead, no one knew.

{name} knows the value of a small beginning.
Big change always started with one trivial-looking payment.

choices.text: Now — focus on actually using what I learned
choices.result_text:
Listening to a course and using it are different.

{name} decided to connect input to output rather than just pile up input.
Learning became an asset only when used.
